title: How does the diagonal of a square split its corners?
description: The diagonal of a square is drawn, and the video finds the two angles it makes with the sides at one corner. Keeko then doubts and gives thirty and sixty, as on a set square.
teaching_notes: One idea: the diagonal of a square makes a triangle with a right angle and two equal sides, so it cuts the corner into two equal angles of forty five degrees. Watch for students who give two unequal angles such as thirty and sixty.

source: In square ABCD the diagonal AC is drawn. Find ∠DAC and ∠DCA.
video_script.why: The child uses the right angle and the two equal sides of a square to see that its diagonal cuts each corner into two equal angles.
video_script.substitution: Take the triangle that the diagonal makes with two sides, share the angles left after the right angle, and use the equal sides to make the shares equal.
video_script.anchor: square ABCD with the diagonal AC drawn and triangle ADC shaded
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the two angles are thirty and sixty, like a set square; but triangle ADC has two equal sides, so its two base angles must be equal.
video_script.payoff_line: Each angle is forty five degrees, so the diagonal cuts each right angle in half

final_answer.spoken: each angle is forty five degrees, so the diagonal cuts each right angle in half

hold_back: the diagonal bisects the right angles
maths_rules: ABCD is a square, so angle ADC = 90 degrees and AD = DC
in triangle ADC, angle DAC + angle DCA = 180 - 90 = 90 degrees
AD = DC, so the angles opposite them are equal: angle DAC = angle DCA
each is 90 / 2 = 45 degrees, so the diagonal bisects the right angles
a set square with 30 and 60 degrees has three different sides, so it does not fit a triangle with two equal sides
video_script.design: One idea: right angle plus two equal sides gives two equal angles of 45 degrees. Wrong idea: the angles are 30 and 60 like a set square. The square with the shaded triangle ADC stays on the board.
